subject: health
unitTitle: Advocacy: Designing a Health Promotion Project
essentialQuestion: What is the smallest change I could actually cause, and how would I know it worked?

prompts.prompt: Explain choosing a scoped, achievable health promotion goal in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of audience analysis and message framing without fear appeals.
Apply accuracy, citation, and avoiding overclaim in advocacy in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving partners, permissions, and realistic constraints; correct it and explain why.
Connect defining a measurable outcome before starting with presenting a proposal and taking critique. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a complete health promotion project proposal — goal, audience, message, partners, constraints, and measurable outcome — for a setting the learner can actually reach. Execution is optional and guardian-approved; the proposal is what is assessed.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The proposal may be written, presented as a slide outline, spoken to an adult, or built on a supplied planning template. No public presentation or published material is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
